section_summary: This section contains correspondence and enclosures about American trade marks, trade names and indications of origin used on Japanese goods. The cases concern Celluloid, Dell, Edison, The Embossing Company, Fostoria and Holeproof Hosiery. State Department replies generally point to private legal proceedings or remedies available after importation, while consular reports investigate particular complaints.

subfiles.title: Celluloid Corporation complaint about Japanese advertisements
subfiles.about: Seeks State Department help against Japanese advertisements using the Celluloid trade mark.
subfiles.summary: O'Brien says a Japanese trade journal circulated in the United States advertises goods as “Celluloid” despite the corporation's registered American mark.

subfiles.title: Reply on the Celluloid complaint
subfiles.about: Explains the legal avenues for contesting use of the Celluloid mark.
subfiles.summary: The Department advises litigation over alleged infringement in the United States. In Japan, registration or proof of an unfair practice would be needed; evidence of exclusive Japanese rights might support an informal inquiry.

subfiles.title: Further request for help concerning Celluloid
subfiles.about: Requests informal action against Japanese firms soliciting American orders as “Celluloid.”
subfiles.summary: O'Brien acknowledges that the mark is unregistered in Japan but cites its longstanding United States registration.

subfiles.title: Reply declining representations in the Celluloid case
subfiles.about: Declines to approach Japan about the advertisements.
subfiles.summary: Without Japanese registration or a United States judicial finding of infringement, the Department sees no basis for representations.

subfiles.title: Post Office Solicitor's Celluloid response
subfiles.about: Explains why a mail fraud order is unavailable on the evidence supplied.
subfiles.summary: Advertisements alone do not establish fraudulent sales through the mails.

subfiles.title: E. Ohashi Shoten celluloid goods sheet
subfiles.about: Advertises celluloid toilet articles with prices and packing quantities.
subfiles.summary: Illustrates mirrors, puff boxes, soap cases and other celluloid wares.

subfiles.title: E. Ohashi Shoten sales letter
subfiles.about: Offers catalogue items and terms for export orders.
subfiles.summary: The firm quotes Tokyo prices, offers samples and sets out payment and shipping terms.

subfiles.title: Postmaster General's inquiry on Celluloid
subfiles.about: Asks whether treaties allow State Department action against Japanese misuse of “Celluloid.”
subfiles.summary: The Post Office finds insufficient evidence for a fraud order.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Postmaster General
subfiles.about: Says State Department action in the Celluloid case is unwarranted.
subfiles.summary: Hull encloses the Department's October 18 reply to O'Brien.

subfiles.title: Postmaster General's acknowledgment
subfiles.about: Acknowledges the Department's position on the Celluloid complaint.
subfiles.summary: The Postmaster General notes that State Department action is unwarranted.

subfiles.title: Dell case jacket
subfiles.about: Identifies the Dell trade mark infringement file.
subfiles.summary: File jacket for Samuel M. Dell & Company's Japanese trade mark case.

subfiles.title: Brush manufacturers' inquiry about the Dell mark
subfiles.about: Asks how to oppose a Japanese application to register “DELL” for brushes.
subfiles.summary: The association reports an impending opposition deadline and seeks procedural advice for its member Samuel M. Dell & Company.

subfiles.title: Advice on opposing Dell registration
subfiles.about: Advises consulting trade mark attorneys about opposition proceedings in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes the apparent two-month opposition period and suggests private counsel determine who should file.

subfiles.title: Reminder requesting a Dell case reply
subfiles.about: Requests a prompt reply before the opposition deadline.
subfiles.summary: The association encloses a copy of its earlier inquiry.

subfiles.title: Copy of the Dell inquiry
subfiles.about: Repeats the request for advice on opposing a Japanese Dell registration.
subfiles.summary: The copy identifies the applicant and the proposed mark for brushes.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of earlier Dell reply
subfiles.about: Sends another copy of the Department's January 2 advice.
subfiles.summary: The Department assumes its original response may already have arrived.

subfiles.title: Edison case jacket
subfiles.about: Identifies the Edison electric lamp trade mark file.
subfiles.summary: File jacket for the Edison case.

subfiles.title: Alexandria report on Edison-marked lamps
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese-made automobile bulbs sold in Egypt under the Edison name.
subfiles.summary: The consul describes the importer and retailer, summarizes inquiries sent to Kobe and Tokyo, and forwards the matter for possible Department action.

subfiles.title: Inquiry to Kobe about Edison-marked lamps
subfiles.about: Requests an investigation of the supplier of Edison-marked bulbs.
subfiles.summary: Blackard compares the Japanese bulbs with genuine Mazda lamps and asks whether the Kobe supplier may use the Edison name.

subfiles.title: Tokyo investigation of Edison mark ownership
subfiles.about: Identifies the Tokyo manufacturer and the Japanese registrant of the Edison mark.
subfiles.summary: Garrels reports that International General Electric holds the Japanese Edison registration for bulbs.

subfiles.title: Instruction forwarding Edison correspondence to Tokyo
subfiles.about: Sends Alexandria's report and the Department's reply for information.
subfiles.summary: Copies of the related Edison correspondence are enclosed.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Alexandria on Edison lamps
subfiles.about: Places the decision on protecting Edison rights with the trade mark owner.
subfiles.summary: The Department assumes International General Electric will decide whether to act.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on Edison lamps
subfiles.about: Summarizes the owner's assessment of remedies for exported Edison-marked lamps.
subfiles.summary: Japanese law appears to offer no remedy when the bulbs are exported without sale in Japan.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch enclosing further Edison correspondence
subfiles.about: Forwards a letter and enclosure concerning Edison-marked lamps in Egypt.
subfiles.summary: Cover despatch for the Tokyo consulate's follow-up correspondence.

subfiles.title: Tokyo letter to Alexandria on Edison enforcement
subfiles.about: Relays International General Electric's view of where action could be taken.
subfiles.summary: The company doubts it can act in Japan against bulbs exported to Egypt and is consulting its Egyptian dealers.

subfiles.title: International General Electric letter on Edison rights
subfiles.about: Explains the company's limited recourse in Japan for export-only bulbs.
subfiles.summary: Fowler believes action, if any, must be taken in Egypt.

subfiles.title: Embossing Company case jacket
subfiles.about: Identifies the file on copied Embossing Company toys and trade names.
subfiles.summary: File jacket for The Embossing Company case.

subfiles.title: White House referral of Greenleaf complaint
subfiles.about: Refers Greenleaf's complaint for consideration.
subfiles.summary: White House routing note sends the matter to the committee.

subfiles.title: White House acknowledgment to Greenleaf
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Greenleaf's letter and its referral to the commercial policy committee.
subfiles.summary: Howe says the President directed the referral.

subfiles.title: Greenleaf complaint about copied toys
subfiles.about: Seeks help stopping Japanese copies of Embossing Company toys before importation.
subfiles.summary: Greenleaf describes copied blocks, puzzles, artwork and the slogan “Toys That Teach.” He asks for Customs or other federal intervention before the goods enter the United States.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Tariff Act Section 337
subfiles.about: Assesses whether Section 337 could address the toy copies before importation.
subfiles.summary: Tariff Commission practice requires actual imports before action.

subfiles.title: Further memorandum on possible remedies
subfiles.about: Reviews Tariff Commission, Federal Trade Commission and treaty possibilities.
subfiles.summary: Officials report that trade remedies ordinarily require imported goods in commerce. The memorandum also identifies the 1911 industrial property convention for further legal review.

subfiles.title: Legal review of the industrial property convention
subfiles.about: Assesses the convention's application to copied Embossing Company toys.
subfiles.summary: No direct treaty remedy appears available; possible unfair-practice proceedings would require ordinary legal action in Japan.

subfiles.title: Sayre letter forwarding a proposed reply
subfiles.about: Sends a proposed response to Greenleaf's complaint.
subfiles.summary: Sayre says no practical remedy appears available before importation.

subfiles.title: Draft White House reply to Greenleaf
subfiles.about: Explains why federal trade remedies cannot prevent anticipated toy imports.
subfiles.summary: The draft describes Section 337 and Federal Trade Commission limits, possible private proceedings in Japan, and the decision against diplomatic representations.

subfiles.title: Howe returns draft reply
subfiles.about: Asks the committee to reply directly to Greenleaf.
subfiles.summary: Howe returns the draft letter.

subfiles.title: Enclosed White House version of proposed reply
subfiles.about: Sets out the proposed White House explanation of available remedies.
subfiles.summary: The text says action under Section 337 or by the Federal Trade Commission depends on importation. It also discusses private action in Japan and declines diplomatic representations.

subfiles.title: Committee reply to Greenleaf
subfiles.about: Reports the committee's conclusion on copied Japanese toys.
subfiles.summary: Sayre explains that Section 337 and Federal Trade Commission remedies depend on actual importation and trade. He declines diplomatic representations and points to ordinary legal channels in Japan.

subfiles.title: Fostoria case jacket
subfiles.about: Identifies the Fostoria trade mark infringement file.
subfiles.summary: File jacket for the Fostoria case.

subfiles.title: Fostoria complaint about Japanese fenders
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese replacement fenders bearing Fostoria marks and parts numbers in India.
subfiles.summary: Zook seeks advice and asks how to protect the planned TiteSeal launch in Asian markets.

subfiles.title: Indian agent's first report on copied fenders
subfiles.about: Reports Japanese fenders bearing numbers resembling Fostoria's.
subfiles.summary: Kothari requests registration details and advice for consulting solicitors.

subfiles.title: Indian agent's second report on copied fenders
subfiles.about: Reports increased orders for Japanese fenders carrying Fostoria marks.
subfiles.summary: Kothari urges immediate action against the imitation products.

subfiles.title: Fostoria TiteSeal promotional brochure
subfiles.about: Promotes TiteSeal compounds and their automotive uses.
subfiles.summary: The illustrated brochure describes light, medium and heavy formulations and shows applications for sealing, lubrication and leak prevention.

subfiles.title: Reply to Fostoria on trade mark protection
subfiles.about: Responds to the fender complaint and plans to register TiteSeal abroad.
subfiles.summary: The Department doubts a remedy is available for unregistered marks, but offers to seek an informal Japanese inquiry if the manufacturer is identified. Commerce is supplying registration guidance.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs note on General Electric protest
subfiles.about: Summarizes an embassy report on a Tokyo protest against General Electric patents.
subfiles.summary: The note mentions antisemitic rhetoric and speculation that it diverted criticism from the United States.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on anti-General Electric meeting
subfiles.about: Reports a Tokyo mass meeting opposing General Electric patent applications.
subfiles.summary: Grew describes the meeting's leaders and attendance. He notes that speakers concentrated on antisemitic attacks while giving little attention to the patent applications, and encloses the group's leaflet.

subfiles.title: Society Opposing the General Electric Patents leaflet
subfiles.from: Society Opposing the General Electric Patents
subfiles.about: Calls for opposition to General Electric's electric bulb patents and litigation.
subfiles.summary: The leaflet lists the society's officers, attacks General Electric and Mazda Lamp, and appeals for support of Japan's bulb industry. It includes antisemitic claims and a protest song.

subfiles.title: Holeproof Hosiery case jacket
subfiles.about: Identifies the Holeproof Hosiery file on Japanese exports.
subfiles.summary: File jacket for the Holeproof Hosiery case.

subfiles.title: Commerce request about “Made in U.S.A.” labels
subfiles.about: Requests the names of Japanese exporters using misleading American origin labels.
subfiles.summary: Commerce asks that the American consul in Hong Kong consult Holeproof Hosiery's agent.

subfiles.title: State Department acknowledgment to Commerce
subfiles.about: Confirms a request to investigate the alleged “Made in U.S.A.” labels.
subfiles.summary: The Hong Kong consul general has been asked to identify exporters, and Commerce will receive the report.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Hong Kong consul general
subfiles.about: Directs an inquiry to Keller and Company about misleading origin labels.
subfiles.summary: The consul general is asked to obtain exporters' names and addresses.

subfiles.title: Hong Kong report on alleged American origin labels
subfiles.about: Traces the report to Japanese-made pencils allegedly sold in Bangkok.
subfiles.summary: Keller's manager recounts a secondhand account of pencils marked “Made in U.S.A.” and mentions “Holesafe” hosiery. He cannot identify the Japanese exporters.

subfiles.title: State Department transmittal to Commerce
subfiles.about: Forwards the Hong Kong report on the alleged misleading labels.
subfiles.summary: The consul's June 11 despatch is enclosed.

subfiles.title: Bangkok investigation of suspect Japanese merchandise
subfiles.about: Investigates claims that Japanese pencils were marked as American goods.
subfiles.summary: The consul finds no evidence of pencils marked “Made in U.S.A.” in Bangkok. He reports seized Japanese imitation pens marked “Made in Germany” and promises to watch for evidence identifying exporters.

subfiles.title: Mallinckrodt cross-reference note
subfiles.about: Points to another file concerning Mallinckrodt's script trade mark in Japan.
subfiles.summary: References a July 18, 1935 Treasury letter and possible narcotics complications.
